methods.label: Rewrite using a common base
methods.explanation:
Both 81 and 3 are powers of 3, so rewriting with that base lets us compare exponents. Since powers of 3 strictly increase as their exponents increase,
\[
3^{x+y}=3^4\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x+y=4.
\]
Also,
\[
81^{x-y}=3^{4(x-y)}=3^1
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x-y=\frac14.
\]
Adding these two linear equations eliminates \(y\); subtracting them eliminates \(x\). Thus
\[
2x=\frac{17}{4},\qquad 2y=\frac{15}{4},
\]
so \(x=17/8\) and \(y=15/8\). Their sum is 4 and their difference is \(1/4\), so they satisfy both original equations. Every transformation was equivalent, making this the unique common solution. It is neither of the pairs in B or C, and it is not an integer pair. Therefore the answer is \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
